intro.title: Module system
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Node.js application that uses the module system to organize code into separate files. You will learn how to export functions and variables from one file and import them into another using `module.exports` and `require`. This introduces the core programming concept of modularity, which helps keep code clean, reusable, and maintainable. The main technologies involved are Node.js's built-in CommonJS module system and JavaScript files. By the end, you'll understand how to structure a basic project with multiple modules.
intro.usecase: The Node.js module system is fundamental to building scalable applications like e-commerce platforms, where product catalog, shopping cart, and payment processing are separate modules. In content management systems, modules organize user authentication, article editing, and media upload functionality. Developers use modules to create reusable components in web servers, API endpoints, and database connectors, enabling clean separation of concerns. This pattern appears in tools like Express.js routers, where each route file is a module handling specific endpoints.
